The patch removes the unused DMA‑32 fallback configuration in the hisi_sas driver, simplifying DMA mask handling because a 64‑bit mask never fails when dev->dma_mask is set.

The patch updates the armada_37xx_wdt driver’s .set_timeout callback to also write the new timeout value to counter 1, which .ping does not modify, ensuring that ioctl(WDIOC_SETTIMEOUT) correctly changes the watchdog timeout.
The patch removes the .is_enabled flag from PRCMU clock drivers because the generic clock core already tracks enable counts, simplifying the driver code.

The patch reorganizes riscv mm init code to remove unnecessary #ifdef CONFIG_XIP_KERNEL directives by moving macros adjacent to related variables and grouping similar cases, reducing conditional compilation clutter.
The patch relaxes the restriction on changing the SCSI target driver database root directory, allowing the change only when no devices are registered, improving configurability during boot.

The patch adds cleanup calls to remove a legacy kprobe_event when add_kprobe_event_legacy() or attach_perf_event fails, preventing leftover events that cause -EBUSY errors when livepatch and kprobe coexist.
The commit adds support for the MediaTek mt8186 SCP in the remoteproc driver, enabling the kernel to manage this processor on the new platform.
The patch adds module parameters to the speakup_dummy driver so its default settings can be specified at boot time, allowing configuration via module options instead of runtime sysfs writes.
Adds legacy compatible string 'riscv,clint0' to the sifive,clint dt-binding so that QEMU‑generated device trees pass dt‑validate, addressing a reported validation error.

The patch updates swiotlb_max_mapping_size() to include the minimum alignment mask in its calculation, fixing the max mapping size computation used by swiotlb_find_slots() so that DMA allocations with non‑zero offsets succeed, resolving boot failures on Hyper‑V Isolation VMs with forced swiotlb.
Switches the Habana Labs CB flow to the new unified memory manager, adding required code and removing the old manager implementation.

The patch changes vmbus_request_addr() to return VMBUS_RQST_ERROR for a zero transaction ID, preventing a NULL cmd_rqst dereference in netvsc_send_completion() and making handling of ID‑0 messages consistent with Hyper‑V semantics.
The commit updates the imx-jpeg driver to handle source changes and enable dynamic resolution changes, refining the related function.

The patch modifies bpf_selem_alloc to use copy_map_value instead of memcpy, preventing the spin‑lock field in certain BPF map values from being incorrectly copied from user space, which fixes initialization errors.
The patch fixes a race condition in MPTCP when processing consecutive ADD_ADDR options by caching the remote address earlier and using the cached value after releasing the PM lock.

The commit separates Zynq DDRC controller bindings from the Synopsys DW uMCTL2 DDRC ECC bindings, updating the DT schema and fixing device descriptions to reflect the different CSR layouts and lack of IRQ support.
The commit modifies the ARM64 Rockchip device tree for ROCK Pi 4 to keep the I2S1 controller disabled, ensuring the pins remain usable as GPIO by default.
The patch adds clock and reset definitions for the ADC block in the Renesas R9A07G043 CPG driver, allowing the kernel to control ADC power and clocking.
The patch deletes the declaration and assignment of the now‑unused variable 'mdss' in drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_drv.c, eliminating a clang -Wunused-but-set-variable warning.
The patch replaces kfree_skb() with kfree_skb_reason() in tcp_v4_rcv(), adding specific drop reason codes (NO_SOCKET, PKT_TOO_SMALL, TCP_CSUM, TCP_FILTER) so freed skbs are logged with the cause.
Removes an obsolete comment and overflow check in highmem dirtyable memory handling after a prior fix guarantees the variable cannot be negative or overflow, simplifying the code.
Updates the MAINTAINERS file for the MediaTek JPEG driver, fixing a broken reference after a yaml conversion and broadening the entry to include the encoder.
The commit modifies the xfs_buf_incore() function to match other buffer APIs, making it return an error code and place the buffer in an output parameter, thus standardising the interface.

The patch adjusts the DSC slice reset logic in the AMD DRM driver so that when neither the minimum nor maximum slice can accommodate the pixel clock, DSC is correctly disabled instead of incorrectly allowing a max slice.
Adds PWM clock and reset entries for channels 8‑14 to the Renesas CPG driver and marks the APB clock as critical, enabling Linux to use these PWM channels.

The patch corrects FDMA MTU handling in the lan966x driver: it now reads the MTU from hardware (including L2 header and FCS) and adjusts skb allocation size to ensure enough space for skb_shared_info, preventing allocation failures when MTU changes.
The patch adds bookkeeping needed to unwind the hypervisor stack in non‑protected nVHE mode on arm64, enabling host‑side stacktrace generation from EL1.
Corrects a misspelled word in the error log printed when devm_snd_dmaengine_pcm_register() fails in the mchp-spdifrx driver.

The patch sets fb_modifiers_not_supported in the virtual KMS driver so vkms reports no modifier support, preventing import‑prime failures and allowing GDM3 to start correctly on AMDGPU virtual displays.
Corrects a Chinese translation in the devicetree usage-model docs, keeping the term 'machine_desc' untranslated.
The patch adds a new helper function in the pmbus hwmon driver to test whether a block register exists, because existing byte‑register checks fail when PEC is enabled.
Replaces the multiline macro vt6655_mac_word_reg_bits_off in the vt6655 driver with an equivalent static inline function to satisfy checkpatch, without changing runtime behavior.
The commit corrects indentation and formatting errors in the sysfs-fs-erofs ABI documentation to eliminate Sphinx build warnings.
The patch adds missing initialization and adjusts H2C data for the BA CAM on the 8852c chipset, fixing incorrect setup that likely caused block‑ack failures.
The commit only adjusts whitespace/indentation in dcn32_hwseq.c to resolve a smatch warning, without changing any code logic or behavior.

Adds handling for independent TX/RX FIFO flush bits in the JZ4740 ASoC driver, flushing each FIFO separately before activation and correcting the previous behavior that left RX unflushed on newer SoCs.
The commit updates the arm64 Qualcomm SM6350 Lena device tree to enable QUP and GPI DMA hardware, preparing the platform for functional I2C nodes.
The commit adds PCI device IDs for Intel Raptor Lake PCH‑S LPSS to the mfd:intel‑lpss driver, enabling the kernel to recognize this new hardware.
Deletes a duplicated word in a comment of the crypto n2 driver, improving the documentation text.

The patch updates the ALSA USB audio driver to enable native DSD playback (up to DSD256) for the Accuphase DAC‑60 by selecting the correct USB alternate setting, which previously lacked auto‑detection.
Adds VCN 4.0 initialization and decoder/encoder ring functions to the amdgpu driver, providing support for the new VCN4 IP block.
Adds EXPORT_SYMBOL for MediaTek VCodec decoder power‑management functions so that, when built as a module, other kernel components can access them.
Adds READ_ONCE() when reading net->ipv4.sysctl_igmp_qrv to avoid concurrent modification races, addressing a data‑race bug in IGMP sysctl handling.
Adds a boolean rx_timeout in the 8250 driver IRQ path to make the timeout condition explicit, without changing behavior, preparing for future reuse.
The patch adds a check for the return value of nvmem_device_find in the PTP OCP driver and handles the IS_ERR() case, preventing misuse of an error pointer.

The patch renames the kernel macro for ID_AA64MMFR2_EL1.VARange from LVA to match the naming in the ARM architecture reference (DDI0487H.a), aligning code with the specification without altering functionality.
Updates comments in the rzg2l thermal driver: replaces unclear wording, fixes a typo, and adjusts comment formatting to match coding style.
The commit removes a duplicated 'the' in a comment at line 807 of powerpc/pseries/vas, fixing a typo without changing code behavior.
The patch removes the unused variable 'cnt' from recv_func in the r8188eu driver, eliminating dead code and simplifying the function.

The patch adds a check for failure to acquire the hardware semaphore in release_swfw_sync, logs an error and aborts, preventing the previously possible infinite loop when hardware is surprise‑removed.
The patch changes generic_map_delete_batch() to call maybe_wait_bpf_programs() once per batch instead of after each deletion, removing redundant synchronize_rcu() barriers and improving efficiency.

Refactors KVM self‑test state_test to use vm_create_with_one_vcpu()/vm_recreate_with_one_vcpu(), passes a struct kvm_vcpu instead of a global VCPU_ID, changes default vCPU ID to 0, and switches to vcpu_run() for clearer test code.
Replaces CONFIG_PM_SLEEP compile‑time guards in the vf610 IIO DAC driver with runtime pm_sleep_ptr() calls, allowing the compiler to omit sleep‑related code when CONFIG_PM_SLEEP is disabled.
The commit updates the copyright year range in the maple_tree test code, extending it to cover the current development year.
The commit updates the rc5t583 MFD driver to use the newer i2c .probe_new() callback, removing the unused i2c_device_id argument.
The patch changes vchiq_get_state in the vchiq_arm driver to return early with NULL when appropriate, and restructures the code to be clearer, improving readability.
The patch moves efi32_pe_entry from head_64.S into the .text section so it can later be compiled as a separate unit, improving code organization.

The patch moves the definitions of ADV7511_REG_CEC_RX_FRAME_HDR and ADV7511_REG_CEC_RX_FRAME_LEN from the public header adv7511.h into the source file adv7511_cec.c, eliminating unused‑variable warnings when the CEC config option is disabled.

The patch adds the CLK_OPS_PARENT_ENABLE flag to pixel and byte clock sources in the Qualcomm SM6350 display clock driver so that the parent clock is enabled before setting the rate, fixing a failure in set_rate.
The patch updates the pcm3168a ASoC driver to replace legacy bus‑clock defines with newer ASoC DAI format terminology, aligning the code with current naming conventions.

Adds runtime verification that the number of IPA commands in a transaction does not exceed the TLV FIFO size on the command channel, by passing a new flag to gsi_channel_data_valid() and checking channel direction.

The patch removes a regular (non‑bit‑field) member that precedes a bit‑field in a packed struct, eliminating unwanted padding that altered the struct size used for zero‑ing and configuration calculations.

The patch fixes a bug where moving VCAP TCAM entries rewrites stale hit counters to hardware, causing inflated statistics. It adds a read‑back of the current counter into tmp->stats.pkts before the migration, ensuring counters are cleared correctly.
The commit deletes a conditional check for IS_SWAPFILE in the NFS code because the macro is always defined, eliminating dead code.
Adjusts tps65219_set_bypass to use .is_enabled() return value for state checking and deletes an unused ret variable, fixing incorrect enable testing.

Adds a transaction ID field to the IPA driver to track the first completed but unpolled transaction, updates it during NAPI polling, and includes temporary sanity‑check warnings that are later removed. Improves internal bookkeeping and debugging.
The commit deletes the tstamp pointer field from the mlx5e_txqsq structure because the timestamp handling was moved to the driver core, making the field obsolete.
The patch changes the NXP NFC driver to suppress a misleading "header length mismatch" log when an I2C transaction fails, returning only the I2C error code.
The commit adds device‑tree bindings required for Wake on Wireless support on the WCN6750 chipset, which uses the ath11k driver.

The patch removes the use of the global ARCH_NR_GPIOS macro in the GPIO aggregator driver, introducing a local constant (512) as the maximum number of GPIOs to aggregate, eliminating dependence on system-wide GPIO count.
The commit reformats comments in the r8188eu driver to match the Linux kernel drivers/net coding style, ensuring consistency before upstream integration.
The commit introduces device‑tree binding documentation for the Renesas RZ/G2L interrupt controller, allowing the kernel to describe and use this hardware in DT files.
The commit updates the r8188eu driver to declare PS_RDY_CHECK as returning a bool, matching its true/false semantics and improving type correctness.
The patch adds a guard in gfs2_glock_dq() to detect if an async glock holder has already been removed from the active/waiting list, preventing a race that could cause a double dequeue.
The patch deletes the driver‑specific yesno() function and replaces its usage with the kernel‑provided str_yes_no() from linux/string_helpers.h, adjusting includes accordingly.
Fixes out-of-bounds array access in the imx-jpeg driver when an error occurs during JPEG parsing, preventing kernel panic on module reload.
The commit adds DT compatible strings for DH electronics i.MX8M Plus DHCOM and PDK2 to the YAML device‑tree binding documentation, enabling kernel support for these new boards.

The patch corrects translate_desc() in the vhost driver by preserving the 'last' argument when repeatedly calling vhost_iotlb_itree_first() inside a loop, ensuring the search range remains constant while 'start' advances.
Adds a guard in lib/cmdline's next_arg to read args[i-1] only when i>0, eliminating an out‑of‑bounds access that caused a page fault when parsing quoted arguments.
The patch reorders functions and static variables in the via686a hwmon driver to eliminate four unnecessary forward declarations, improving code structure without altering behavior.

The patch modifies acpi_processor_get_platform_limit() to compare the new _PPC value with the previously stored one and only update the frequency QoS request when it differs; it also validates the value against the state count and sets a consistent default in acpi_processor_ppc_init().
The commit removes the build‑system hack that forced head.o to be linked first on arm64, relying on the linker script to place the .head.text header correctly.
The patch updates the Tegra194 PCI driver to compute the RAS DES PCIe capability offset at runtime rather than using hard‑coded values for each controller, improving maintainability.
Adds a per‑frontend pause flag and changes backend state transitions so that when all active streams are paused the backend moves to PAUSE instead of STOP, correcting resource management.

The patch adds infrastructure to record each module that, when unloaded, contributed a taint to the kernel, keeping a count and optionally displaying them. It introduces new data structures and hooks, disabled by default.

The patch restricts the /proc/powerpc/ofdt interface on pseries systems so that when kernel lockdown is active, only trusted firmware‑provided device‑tree updates are allowed, blocking user‑space modifications that could write arbitrary physical addresses.
The commit updates ADI ASoC drivers to use the new legacy DAI naming flag, switching from opting‑in to the new naming scheme to opting‑out, aligning drivers with the new naming convention.
The patch replaces kzalloc(x*y) with kcalloc(y, x) in ptp_ocp, leveraging kcalloc's overflow checks to allocate arrays more safely.
The patch removes the unused regs field from coredump_params because it always equals task_pt_regs(current), simplifying the code.
The patch adds a missing dma_release_channel() call in the probe error path of the sun4i-emac driver, ensuring the DMA channel allocated by emac_configure_dma() is released if probing fails.
The patch modifies btrfs_ioctl to obtain the inode from the file and reuse it for callbacks, eliminating the need to create a separate inode instance.
The patch replaces a hand‑rolled extraction of match data in acpi_smbus_cmi_add() with the standard device_get_match_data() helper, cleaning up the code.
Adds a helper rdev_mdlock_deref() that wraps rcu_dereference_protected() for rdev/replacement pointer accesses under mddev_lock, annotating safety and silencing sparse warnings in md/raid5.

The commit adds handling for GTP_ECHO_REQ packets in the kernel GTP driver, sending a GTP_ECHO_RSP with appropriate information elements, to satisfy the GTP specification when no userspace daemon is present.
Adds a NULL check for hdev before accessing hdev->name in Bluetooth logging helpers, preventing kernel oops when hdev is invalid.

The patch swaps cpumask_next_* calls for cpumask_first_* when the start index is zero, adds a missing cpumask_first_zero() helper, and updates related code, improving readability and efficiency without altering behavior.
The commit marks the Clevo‑mail LED driver as broken because it uses brightness to control blink rate, which is unconventional, and notes that a proper interface fix is pending.
The patch checks the result of a BSS lookup in nl80211; if the pointer is an error (IS_ERR()), it replaces it with NULL to avoid freeing an error pointer later.

The patch modifies the Aquantia PHY driver to clear default advertisement of 2.5G and 5G speeds when the Ethernet port is limited to 1 Gbps, ensuring the PHY only advertises speeds up to 1000BASE‑T as requested.
Adds missing rcu_read_lock and takes a reference to real_dev in bond_ethtool_get_ts_info, fixing a crash when the function is invoked via setsockopt without holding RCU lock.
Adds logging for all codec quirks (SSP, GPIO, DMIC) in the Intel SOF ASoC driver, extending previous logging that only covered SSP.
The patch renames the misspelled fields maxpctksize and maxpcktsize in the USB gadget f_uac2 driver to wMaxPacketSize, aligning with the USB specification and improving code consistency.

The patch updates perf data's JSON conversion to emit tracepoint probe variables as JSON fields using tep_print_field, so outputs now include entries like "__probe_ip" and other probe data that were previously omitted.
Corrects misspelled words in nvmet-auth warning and debug log messages, improving readability and professionalism of kernel logs.
The commit corrects a typographical error in a comment within the drm/amd driver, replacing "the the" with "the".

The patch refactors conv_uni_to_pc() in the consolemap code to improve readability by caching a pointer, adding a null‑check, splitting a large conditional into smaller ones, and removing an extraneous newline.
Adds a MAINTAINERS entry for the Allwinner A31 MIPI CSI-2 bridge driver, documenting the new maintainer.
The commit adds a control mapping override in the uvcvideo driver for two Chicony Easycamera USB IDs to limit the power line control, because those devices implement the control incorrectly.
The patch corrects HDMI ODM combine mode handling in AMD DRM, stopping unnecessary stream reprogramming that caused intermittent black screens.
The patch removes the unit address from the panel endpoint node in the am335x device tree, fixing a compilation error caused by a missing required 'reg' property.
The patch updates the hisilicon DRM driver to initialize on‑stack mode structures with drm_mode_init(), ensuring list heads are cleared and avoiding residual stack data.
The patch replaces direct uncore register accesses in i915 display power code with intel_de_* accessor functions, centralising register handling.
Adds runtime checks in amdgpu discovery to ensure the number of VCN and SDMA instances reported by firmware does not exceed the driver‑defined limits, preventing out‑of‑range accesses.

The patch modifies the s390 extable handling so that the amode31 exception table is sorted earlier, ensuring the early program‑check handler can locate its entries. This prevents missing extable entries when a program check occurs before the normal sorting point.
Removes the reset_resume callback in the xpad driver so that after suspend/resume the USB core rebinds wireless Xbox 360 controllers, fixing LED and force‑feedback failures.
Patch makes fb_modesetting_disabled() a static‑inline function in the header, removing multiple definition linker errors when compiled into fbmon.o and fbmem.o.
The commit extends the lan743x network driver to handle Clause‑45 MDIO PHY management, enabling communication with PHYs using the Clause‑45 protocol.
Adds a stub pfn.h header with definitions needed by test code, allowing the tests to compile.

The patch stops calling acpi_video_set_dmi_backtype() in the Toshiba ACPI driver, preventing unwanted unregistration of the acpi_video backlight and the resulting udev race, and adds DMI quirks for the two known transflective-display models.

The patch deletes the driver’s call to the dtim_assoc IOVAR in brcmfmac, which was always failing because recent firmware no longer supports it, thus stopping the repeated “wl dtim_assoc failed (-52)” messages after a roam.

The patch replaces BUG_ON() with WARN_ON_ONCE() in signal handling, so that when an unexpected condition occurs the kernel logs a warning and continues instead of panicking, improving debuggability and stability during development.
The patch removes redundant false initializations of three boolean flags in update_recvframe_phyinfo_88e of the r8188eu driver, as they are overwritten before use.
The commit rewrites shmem_read_mapping_page_gfp() to call shmem_get_folio_gfp() instead of manually handling compound pages, reducing extra compound_head() calls and streamlining the code.
Adds a check on NTFS BOOT sectors_per_clusters shift value, returning -EINVAL when out of range to avoid negative or oversized shifts that caused a UBSAN shift‑out‑of‑bounds error.

The patch removes the pfn_to_page call from kasan_early_init, preventing a null mem_section dereference that occurs when KASAN and SPARSEMEM are enabled without SPARSE_VMEMMAP, thus fixing the boot‑time crash.

The patch makes the dpaa2‑eth driver reuse a cached scatter‑gather table for normal packets, enlarges the cache buffers, and replaces per‑packet allocate/free with get/recycle calls, improving memory handling.
The commit changes the dt-bindings maintainer entry to use Krzysztof Kozlowski's kernel.org email address, updating contact information in the documentation.
Adds a new enum value "skip" to the qcom,gsi-loader property in dt-bindings, allowing devices to indicate that GSI firmware is already loaded and should not be loaded by AP or modem.
The patch changes the SDM630 device tree to describe the TCSR mutex using MMIO instead of a syscon regmap, adding the required 'reg' property and satisfying DT schema checks.

Fixes a bug where returning from an interrupt to a soft‑masked (irqs‑disabled) context could lose a pending soft‑masked IRQ because the code incorrectly follows the exit path for irqs‑enabled contexts, clearing the wrong flag. Adds a comment explaining the correct behavior.

The commit disables creation of the /sys/.../online control file for all I/O master CPUs on LoongArch by marking them non‑hotpluggable, preventing user‑space tools from seeing a misleading hotplug interface.
The patch removes the unused variable 'last' and dead code from remove_siblinginfo() in the IA‑64 architecture, simplifying the function.
Switches the arm64 selftest Makefile to use TEST_GEN_PROGS_EXTENDED instead of TEST_PROGS_EXTENDED, ensuring generated programs are built correctly while leaving script-based tests unchanged.
The patch adds rollback logic in fbcon when vc_resize() fails, restoring the previous font size to avoid inconsistent state, addressing a syzbot‑reported page‑fault bug.
The commit updates the Media DT binding for MediaTek video encoder by documenting a new "power-domains" property, allowing encoders to be linked to a power domain in device trees.
The commit lowers the log severity of power and thermal envelope events to INFO, treating them as informational messages rather than warnings or errors.
The commit updates device‑tree binding files for Hirschmann Hellcreek network devices to reference other schemas using absolute paths instead of relative ones, improving consistency and readability.
The patch adds EXPORT_SYMBOL declarations for mt6358 driver functions that were missing, resolving undefined symbol errors when the driver is built as a loadable module.
The commit reorders fields in the LTTPR UHBR link‑rate support struct to follow the DP2.0 specification, updating the code to match the spec’s defined layout.
The patch adds an early‑return in the wcd9335 slimbus mux put function so it does not report a value change when the value is unchanged, eliminating spurious events.

The patch moves the acquisition of card->lock earlier in fw_core_handle_bus_reset so that accesses to card->local_node and card->bm_retries are protected, and adjusts fw_destroy_nodes calls accordingly, adding a clarifying comment.

The patch moves the _set_policy function into the chip_ops structure for the RTL8852C driver, reorganizing code to accommodate additional firmware‑supported policies such as DBCC, multi‑role, and TDMA.
The commit deletes an unnecessary assignment to the variable 'negative' in ad2s1210.c, eliminating a dead store that clang flagged, without altering runtime behavior.
The patch modifies the octeontx2 PF driver to stop stripping error codes from AF replies and instead forwards those replies unchanged to the VF, enabling the VF to receive the error codes set by AF.
The patch removes an unnecessary flags check for CHIP_IP_DISCOVERY in the amdgpu DRM driver because IP‑based discovery is now always available, simplifying the code path.

The patch modifies the DW HDMI driver to send General Control Packets only when the sink supports Deep Color, disabling automatic GCP for 24‑bit color on non‑Deep‑Color sinks, aligning behavior with HDMI 1.4b spec.
The patch modifies the ARM IRQ handler to stop using register R9, preserving its value for the entry/exit code that relies on it for the task pointer.
Updates the AMD DRM display driver to use VSC packet revision 4 (rev2 for PSR1) as required by PSRSU, following the eDP 1.5 spec and revising Start/End SDP data.
The commit updates tools/tracing/Makefile to add build, install and clean targets for the rtla component, allowing it to be compiled and managed alongside other tracing tools.
Adds a compatible string entry for the PCA85073A RTC in the PCF85063 driver, enabling the driver to recognize and support this hardware variant.

The patch sets the parent pointer of a USB‑PD partner object to its associated Type‑C device using the partner registration wrapper, enabling the PD object to be linked back to the correct Type‑C port.
Adds device‑tree nodes for an MMIO‑based MDIO multiplexer on the ls1043a‑qds board, defines a simple‑mfd compatible for the FPGA, and connects Ethernet interfaces to the new PHY nodes.

The patch moves the IEEE80211_VHT_CAP_TX_ANTENNA_PATTERN and RX_ANTENNA_PATTERN settings into the stream initialization of the mt76 driver to ensure antenna configuration is present for 6 GHz capability.
The patch adds a gfp_t parameter to convert_context() and its wrapper, allowing callers to choose GFP_KERNEL or GFP_ATOMIC, fixing a BUG where sleeping was invoked inside a spin lock.
The patch adds a shutdown() callback registration for the WCN6750 Wi‑Fi device in the ath11k driver so that DMA stops before the SMMU driver is shut down, avoiding SMMU translation faults.

The patch enables configuring bridge port flags on the NPI port of the mscc ocelot driver, redirecting flag handling to the analyzer block index for the CPU port, so the Felix DSA driver can control flooding to its CPU port.
Adds a new compatible string for MSM8974 to the qcom,msm8916-mss-pil device tree binding, handling the extra mss-supply property with a simple conditional.
Adds a null‑pointer check in dc_submit_i2c_oem and aborts the call when ddc is NULL, preventing a crash in the AMD DRM display driver.

The commit removes the i.MX8QM entry from the fsl-lpuart compatible enum in dt-bindings, because the hardware is compatible with i.MX8QXP, forcing nodes to list both strings via the existing items entry.

The patch moves removal of i915_gem_context from the contexts list to after the final reference is dropped, fixing a race that caused a general protection fault in i915_perf. It also corrects spin_lock usage and drops unused cleanup.
The patch adds a helper that allocates MSI‑X interrupt vectors for vDPA ifcvf devices, handling both virtqueue and configuration interrupts.
The patch removes a snd_BUG_ON() check in snd_usbmidi_output_open() because a NULL port can legitimately occur due to malformed USB descriptors, causing unnecessary kernel BUGs reported by syzbot.

The patch modifies the Sony laptop driver to skip probing the keyboard backlight when the hardware lacks a separate probe address, preventing the probe from unintentionally turning off the backlight (0x153).

The patch restricts 36‑bpp linebuffer usage to DCN display engines, forcing DCE engines to use 30‑bpp, eliminating dithering bugs on DCE‑11.2 hardware and restoring correct pixel passthrough for scientific workloads.
The patch renames an inner variable in mac80211's airtime code to avoid shadowing the outer 'rate' variable, improving code clarity without altering functionality.

The patch updates x86/boot assembly code to wrap literal address casts with the absolute_pointer() macro, avoiding GCC 11/12 -Warray-bounds warnings caused by treating literal pointers as offset pointers.
Adds hardware definitions for LEDs and buttons of the Asus RTN-10U router in the BCM47XX MIPS driver, allowing the kernel to detect and control these components.

The patch marks irq_chip structures as immutable in pinctrl actions, removes an unnecessary copy, adds IRQCHIP_IMMUTABLE flag and helper calls to gpiolib, eliminating kernel warnings about mutable chips.
The commit updates the imx8mp-phycore-som device tree to disable unused LDO4 and enable LDO5, which supplies VSEL for the SD‑Card bus, correcting the power‑regulator configuration.

Updates the Microchip PIT64B timer driver to use mchp_pit64b_suspend() and mchp_pit64b_resume() for disabling/enabling timer clocks during init and removal, removing direct clk_prepare_{disable,enable} calls and aligning with existing clockevent state handling.
The patch updates i915 microcode filename macros to handle underscores and dots uniformly via the concatenation macro, removing explicit delimiters in prefixes and simplifying macro logic.
Adds a snd_card_free() call in the probe error path of the sonicvibes ALSA driver to correctly release resources before card registration, fixing a cleanup bug.
Adds a DMA engine driver for the Apple ADMAC found in Apple Silicon SoCs, integrating it into the dmaengine subsystem.
The patch changes the udl driver to pass a rectangle structure directly to udl_handle_damage(), removing intermediate handling for simpler code.
Adds extra selftest cases for bpf btf_dump to check padding handling, using handcrafted and fuzz‑generated inputs.
Adds a call to unregister_candev() in mcp251x_can_probe() when gpio setup fails, ensuring proper cleanup of the CAN device on probe error.

The commit adjusts the indentation of a bullet list in Documentation/ABI/testing/sysfs-class-thermal to satisfy Sphinx formatting rules, eliminating a build warning about missing blank line after the list.

The commit updates the Verdin i.MX8MP device tree to expose the USB_1 over‑current detection pin (active‑low) and removes its previous gpio_hog mapping, enabling hardware‑level over‑current monitoring.
Adds handling for CMD_ERROR_EVENT in the kvaser_usb leaf driver to safely process an error event that indicates a driver misbehaviour, preventing undefined behaviour.
Adds the _EL1 suffix to macro definitions for ID_AA64ISAR2_EL1 register fields to follow naming conventions; no functional changes.

The patch updates the egress rate‑limit configuration for CN10K hardware, correcting the NIX_AF_TLXX_PIR/CIR register format, burst exponent/mantissa handling, and changes the maxrate field from 32‑bit to 64‑bit to match the stack.
The patch replaces BUG_ON with WARN_ON in the sfc driver and adds recovery handling, turning a fatal kernel panic into a warning with graceful cleanup, and also silences a checkpatch warning.
The patch makes the uid_strings const array static instead of stack‑allocated, eliminating per‑call allocation and slightly reducing object size.
The patch defines a constant for the fixed value 0x6 and removes the now‑unused UsbTxAggDescNum member from struct hal_data_8188e, cleaning up the data structure.
The patch updates uml_vector_default_bpf() to accept a const MAC address pointer, matching recent constification of MAC address structures and fixing compilation errors.
The patch renames the testmode antenna configuration fields from chainmask to antenna_mask for both bands, removing conversion logic when sending firmware commands and simplifying user configuration.

The patch clears the page->private field after allocating a page for compaction or after splitting a huge page, fixing cases where PG_private was cleared but folio->private remained non‑NULL, which caused filesystem bugs.
The commit corrects a spelling mistake in a comment of the ASoC AMD ACP driver, changing the typo to proper spelling without altering any code behavior.
The commit adds constant definitions for the Mediatek Ethernet PCS, based on investigation, to enable handling of this hardware in the driver.

The patch updates the fbdev hot‑unplug workaround for framebuffers without a device, adding a warning message and revising comments to note that the workaround should no longer be triggered now that OF framebuffers have platform devices.
The commit modifies the f2fs driver to treat the whole zoned device as having a single capacity, removing per‑zone capacity handling to simplify the code.
The commit updates all source files to replace the GPLv2 license boilerplate with the SPDX identifier "GPL-2.0-only", standardizing license declarations across the tree.
The patch deletes an unused declaration of sni_cpu_time_init() in the MIPS time code, as all calls were removed earlier, eliminating dead code.
The patch makes the AMD display driver increase the compositor buffer size before updating clocks, fixing P‑State hangs caused by the previous ordering.
Adds a pinctrl controller node to the MT6795 device tree, exposing the hardware block for future pin configuration in machine-specific DTS files.
The commit corrects various spelling mistakes in the ath10k Wi‑Fi driver source and comments, as flagged by the codespell tool. No functional code changes are introduced.
The patch removes a redundant resource check from the c67x00 USB driver's remove() routine because the probe() already validates the resource.

The patch updates KVM x86 documentation for MSR filtering, rephrasing text, correcting terminology, removing redundant sections, and fixing an off‑by‑one error in the described range. No code changes are introduced.
The patch changes the memory‑management code to use folio_swap_flags directly instead of converting a folio to a page and then calling page_swap_flags, because the caller already works with folios.
The commit updates the error message shown when LRO state modification fails, replacing the old specific text with a more generic name, improving clarity without altering functionality.
Implements support for nested VMLOAD and VMSAVE instructions in KVM's x86 nSVM, enabling proper handling of these VM exits when running multiple nested Linux guests.
The patch modifies the Cadence SoundWire driver to stop overwriting msg->buf during write commands, ensuring the caller's buffer remains unchanged as it should be read‑only.
The commit adds a temporary variable for struct device in the intel_soc_pmic_bxtwc driver, refactoring the code to be cleaner and more readable.
Moves local variables of dml32_CalculateSwathAndDETConfiguration into a dummy struct, shrinking the function's stack frame.
The commit reorganizes and cleans up the Chinese admin‑guide documentation, reformatting the HTML To‑Do list and adjusting the directory index for clearer presentation.
The patch moves the TSC‑ratio macros/definitions used by the AMD SVM KVM implementation from a source file into svm.h, matching the SVM spec and improving code organization.
Adds a documentation file describing the device tree bindings for the Renesas RZ/G2UL USB2 PHY, noting it matches the RZ/G2L PHY and uses the existing compatible string.
The commit refactors the ltc2983 temperature driver to use generic device properties, removing dependence on OF and allocating buffers for all values at once, enabling use on non‑OF platforms.
Adds an alternate pin multiplexing configuration for DCMI pins in the STM32 device tree to support the AV96 board.
The commit reverts a previous sbitmap change that fixed batched wait_cnt accounting because it caused CPU stalls and infinite loops; restoring the old code eliminates the regression.
The patch deletes the q->qid field from the mt76 driver because it is no longer referenced, cleaning up dead code.
Commit fixes a potential use‑after‑free in moxart_remove() by saving the device base register before freeing the MMC host and using that saved value instead of dereferencing the freed pointer.
The patch ensures the sta.mlo flag is set when a station uses Multi‑Link Operation, fixing a missing assignment introduced by earlier changes.
Adds minimal register set (regset) definitions for the m68k architecture, enabling coredump support in the elf_fdpic loader. The changes are conditional and limited to the required definitions.
The commit adds the V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_MODIFY_LAYOUT flag to the imx319 i2c driver control that changes Bayer order when flips are applied, correcting the control definition.
Changes process_msg_close in rnbd-srv to return void instead of int because it always returned 0, removing an unnecessary return value.
Implements the SBI v0.3 System Reset (SRST) extension for RISC‑V KVM guests, adding standard poweroff and reboot interfaces as defined by the specification.

Adds 16‑byte NOP padding before every function on x86, aligning functions to 16 bytes and inserting extra space for future software call‑stack tracking and kCFI/FineIBT, with negligible performance impact.
The patch renames the clock identifier video_pll1 to video_pll in the i.MX driver to match the reference manual, keeping old constants for compatibility and making no functional changes.
The patch replaces a custom single_enabled_crtc() implementation in i9xx_update_wm() with the standard helper used elsewhere, and removes an unused 'enabled' variable, simplifying the code.

Adds a runtime check before entering MALL Sub‑Stream to ensure a PSR panel has already entered PSR, and avoids overwriting link settings when programming a phantom stream, preventing incorrect state handling.
The patch changes the audit_init_parent() function to treat the path argument as a const pointer, preventing modifications and improving code safety and readability.
The commit modifies the ASoC tas2770 driver to accept mono audio streams, enabling downmix and channel switching for a mono speaker amp.
The patch changes the STM32 VREFBUF regulator driver to call pm_runtime_resume_and_get instead of pm_runtime_get_sync, aiming to simplify the power‑management flow.

The patch changes the Intel raw NAND driver to obtain the chip‑select GPIO from the flash device tree node (child of the NAND controller) instead of the controller node, correcting the source of the CS line.
The patch replaces XFS inode fork size macros with static inline functions, providing type‑checked helpers instead of macro expansions, improving safety and readability.

The commit corrects hci_read_buffer_size_sync to stop using the LE‑only opcode HCI_OP_LE_READ_BUFFER_SIZE_V2 and instead rely on the proper hci_le_read_buffer_size_sync path, fixing a functional error.
The patch modifies the 8188EU driver to allocate the efuse buffer with kmalloc and free it on exit, replacing a fixed 512‑byte stack array and dropping the __aligned(4) qualifier.
The patch changes several functions in dcn32_hubbub.c to static scope because they are only used within that file, eliminating unused‑function warnings and improving encapsulation.
The commit revises the PTP OCP driver to compute sysfs attribute groups before registration and creates them in one call, avoiding removal of unregistered groups that caused a kernel crash.
The patch deletes the declaration of intel_gt_create_kobj() from the i915 GT driver because the function is never used, cleaning up dead code.

The patch modifies the max9759 driver Kconfig to stop unconditionally selecting the gpiolib subsystem, because GPIO usage is optional, thereby eliminating unnecessary build-time dependencies and warnings in random configurations.
Adds folio_batch_move_lru() and related helpers, converting LRU handling from pagevecs to folio_batches, establishing new infrastructure for future patches.
The patch deletes an unneeded f2fs_lock_op call in f2fs_new_inode because allocation functions no longer need checkpoint blocking and other locks already protect the relevant data.
Adds an is_subset helper to the perf cpumap code, returning true when the second cpumap is a subset of the first.

The commit adds explicit include directives that were missing in the lynxpoint pinctrl driver and orders all header includes alphabetically, improving code clarity and ensuring required symbols are available.
The patch deletes tcf_connmark_walker and tcf_connmark_search from the net scheduler because they duplicate generic walk/search utilities, simplifying the code.
Updates the Nouveau TU102 driver to send the high 32 bits during sw_bundle64_init, correcting a missing field that broke proper initialization.
Updates the rkvdec driver to use the new vb2_find_buffer API for retrieving a vb2_buffer by timestamp, replacing previous lookup code.
The commit adds new unit tests for the mctp driver to verify key/tag lookup behavior on routed packets, inserting specific entries and checking match/mismatch outcomes.

The patch adds a manual snd_card_free() call in the cs46xx ALSA driver’s probe error path to correctly release resources before card registration, fixing a resource‑leak bug caused by devres cleanup ordering.
Replaces custom error handling in the mxsfb DRM driver with the dev_err_probe() helper, adding a hint in /sys/kernel/debug/devices_deferred.
The patch changes bootmem code to use the page->index field instead of page->freelist, eliminating pointer casts and using an integer that holds the same bits.
The commit updates the sdw-mockup driver to use the new snd_sdw_params_to_config helper for converting hw_params to SoundWire configuration, simplifying the conversion logic.
Fixes a memory leak in configfs_create_dir() by correcting refcount handling on error paths, adding a configfs_put() call to release resources.
The patch updates xdp_do_redirect() error codes for AF_XDP redirects, using ENOMEM for allocation failures and ENOBUFS for Rx‑buffer‑full, enabling drivers to differentiate these situations.
The patch changes nvme-pci reset handling so that on reset failure the driver is no longer unbound; instead the controller is shut down and left in a dead state.
Adds missing unevaluatedProperties/additionalProperties = false to child node schemas in opp dt-bindings, tightening validation so only documented properties are accepted.
The patch adds a missing uid release (put_uid) when __io_sqe_files_scm() finds no files, preventing a memory leak in io_uring's file registration cleanup.

The commit updates the ARM AES‑NEON‑based CBC crypto configuration to also enable the generic CBC and AES algorithms as fallbacks, ensuring the __cbc-aes-neonbs algorithm can register during boot even when its specific implementation is unavailable.

Adds a validation in the ASoC core that checks the driver field of snd_ctl_card_info; if the driver name is set via the legacy wrapping method (truncating to 15 chars), it now prints an error, urging drivers to use proper names and avoid clashes.
Adds a board configuration (adl_rt5682) to enable the alc5682 headset codec on Intel platforms that lack a speaker amplifier, connecting it to SSP0 per Intel BT offload design.
The patch removes the unused gfp_flags argument from null_alloc_page() in the null_blk driver, updating callers to use the fixed GFP_NOIO value, simplifying the API.

Implements a minimal sysfs stub for DAMON, replacing the debugfs interface with a directory/file hierarchy to control virtual address space monitoring, laying groundwork for a new user‑space interface.
Adds a NET dependency to the INTEL_HFI_THERMAL Kconfig entry so it aligns with THERMAL_NETLINK's NET requirement, removing a Kconfig warning and 48 build errors.

The commit corrects the bitmask definitions in the RX_DMA_GET_SPORT and RX_DMA_GET_SPORT_V2 macros of the MediaTek Ethernet driver, swapping the masks that were previously reversed, ensuring proper extraction of the source port from DMA descriptors.

The patch corrects the prefetch calculation loop for DCN3.2 in the AMD DRM driver by resetting local variables each iteration, ensuring the loop exits correctly instead of consuming the entire vstartup after a failure.

The patch addresses a race condition in roccat_read() where a report buffer can be freed while copy_to_user is accessing it, leading to a use‑after‑free. It adds proper synchronization to prevent the premature kfree.

The commit removes the unused CONFIG_DRM_AMD_DC_DCN macro from the amdgpu_dm directory, cleaning up redundant configuration that was only used to bypass compilation errors, aligning DC code to be OS-agnostic.
The patch changes mac80211 code so that when the DTIM period is set, it is stored in link->conf->dtim_period and not cleared, while still using beacon data when present.
Adds the list_for_each_table_entry macro to the proc sysctl code to simplify and tidy traversal of ctl_table structures, improving readability and maintainability.

The patch changes io_uring's multishot accept handling to drop pending accept requests when the completion queue overflows, mirroring multishot poll behavior, thereby correcting ordering problems that could cause incorrect accept processing.
The patch restores correct speed negotiation for CPU/DSA ports in the mv88e6xxx DSA driver by fetching port capabilities early, fixing the default 10 Mbps speed caused by missing mac_capabilities.

The patch updates ath10k driver source to silence recent checkpatch warnings by replacing strlcpy with strscpy and fixing an unnecessary integer promotion in a printf format, without altering functionality.
The commit updates the device‑tree bindings for the ITE it66121 HDMI bridge to include audio support, adding new properties and documentation for audio handling.
Adds a check in io_uring networking code to reject zerocopy sendmsg calls on sockets that do not support zerocopy, mirroring earlier handling for send requests.
Adds support for the ethtool –identify option in the nfp driver, enabling the NIC firmware to blink the panel LED when requested.
Adds a new device tree binding header for the Himax hx83112b touchscreen, enabling kernel to describe this hardware in DT files.
The commit adds a regulator node and enables the PCIe 2 controller and its combphy in the quartz64-b device tree, extending the board's hardware description to support PCIe 2.

The patch separates nvme_kill_queues into two parts: a new function nvme_mark_namespaces_dead that only marks namespaces dead, and moves the queue unquiescing logic to the callers, improving code clarity and modularity.

The patch deletes an unnecessary condition that checks for Correctable Error (CE) status when querying RAS error addresses in the amdgpu DRM driver, because only Uncorrectable Error (UE) addresses are currently queried.
The commit resolves sparse static analysis warnings in PowerPC time code by adding missing declarations, including proper headers, removing duplicate symbols, and reordering definitions.
The patch replaces duplicated enable/disable code in the Merrifield GPIO driver with a call to the existing str_enable_disable() helper, simplifying the implementation.
Updates the kerneldoc-preamble script to test for xeCJK.sty before loading, preventing LaTeX errors on systems lacking the texlive-xecjk package.

The patch replaces struct sockaddr with struct sockaddr_storage in NFS server structures and updates memcpy calls to use the larger size, eliminating false positive Fortify warnings about field‑spanning writes.
The patch updates Btrfs code to replace uses of INT_LIMIT(loff_t) with the more self‑describing macro OFFSET_MAX, improving readability without changing semantics.
The commit deletes the obsolete of_gpio.h header in the zevio GPIO driver and updates code to use the newer of_* alternatives, adjusting function calls and structures accordingly.

The patch modifies the amdkfd driver to enforce pairwise contiguous CU masking and round‑robin distribution across shader engines, assuming WGP mode, correcting incorrect CU mask handling on GPUs with work‑group processors.
Replace custom delayed‑work handling in the max14656 power‑supply driver with devm_delayed_work_autocancel(), reducing code size and using managed resources.
Adds a new hardware capability flag (FEAT_MTE3) for ARM64 MTE asymmetric mode, exposing it to userspace via the hwcap mechanism.
The patch extracts combo PHY register definitions from the generic i915 register pool into a dedicated header, limiting their inclusion to files and platforms that actually need them.
The patch changes the Palmas MFD driver to call device_get_match_data() directly, removing manual match‑data handling and simplifying the driver code.
The commit replaces custom 64‑bit I/O code in the ptp_pch driver with the generic ioread64_hi_lo() / iowrite64_hi_lo() helpers, improving portability and code reuse.
The commit deletes the sx8 block driver source files, removing support for an obsolete hardware driver that has been unmaintained since 2005.

The commit updates the device-tree binding documentation for Qualcomm USB VBUS regulators, renaming the example node from “dcdc” to the more appropriate “usb-vbus-regulator”. No code changes, only documentation.
Adds the UNTRAIN_RET mitigation to the Xen entry point on x86, ensuring the return predictor is cleared when entering Xen, a security hardening measure.
Removes the obsolete <linux/gpio.h> header from the i2c/ccs driver, which already includes <linux/gpio/consumer.h>, eliminating an unused include.
Patch modifies kbuild's header_check script to stop checking include/linux/cyclades.h, which now intentionally warns if included, preventing spurious warnings.

The commit adds the ability to specify a different device for DMA mapping in the mt76 driver, enabling WED support that needs non‑coherent DMA while the PCI device may be set for coherent DMA. The driver will adjust the PCI HIF coherent IO setting on attach.
The patch renames the function btrfs_insert_file_extent() to btrfs_insert_hole_extent() and drops unused parameters, updating all call sites accordingly. It clarifies intent and simplifies the API.

The patch adds proper freeing of the debug_help_string buffer allocated in orangefs_prepare_debugfs_help_string(), ensuring it is released on module removal and when the string is updated, thus eliminating a kmemleak.
The commit updates the Qualcomm ADSP remoteproc device-tree binding docs, simplifying interrupt constraints because variants differ only by an optional last interrupt.
The patch increases the GT reset failure timeout from 5 s to 60 s in the i915 driver, preventing premature device wedge and allowing more diagnostics when a reset hangs.
The commit adds handling for PTP timestamping interrupts in the sparx5 network driver, enabling software to read timestamps from the FIFO when hardware signals completion.
Adds a new requires_cpu flag to perf's uncore event handling, separating it from system_wide because uncore events must be tied to a specific CPU.
Adds kernel documentation strings for core domain fields in the Tegra PMC driver, enabling kerneldoc generation. No functional code changes.
Adds a null‑pointer check after platform_get_resource() in the mt6397 RTC driver to avoid dereferencing a NULL pointer.
The commit renames the existing filter group identifiers to include "vlan" for better readability, distinguishing them from upcoming QinQ group names.
The patch deletes the now‑unused declaration of arch_kprobe_override_function() from the x86/kprobes code after earlier changes removed all its callers, cleaning up dead code.

Wraps the -mno-branch-likely flag in a cc-option test for MIPS Loongson targets, so clang’s unsupported flag no longer triggers a -Werror failure, and moves the test to Kconfig to run at configuration time, reducing build overhead.
The patch replaces of_irq_get_byname with fwnode_irq_get_byname in platform code, allowing named interrupts to be obtained from both OF and ACPI devices via the fwnode abstraction.
Adds a new helper function hda_codec_device_remove() to the Intel SOF ASoC HDA codec driver, continuing the split between controller and codec responsibilities.
The commit introduces new mmhub v3_0_1 header files to the drm/amdgpu driver, updating the codebase to support the newer hardware version that differs from v3_0_0.
The patch replaces a sprintf call with snprintf in ptp_ocp_verify(), improving code readability and safety without altering functionality.
The patch rewrites devm_clk_hw_register_clkdev() to use devm_add_action_or_reset() instead of manual devres allocation and addition, simplifying the code without altering functionality.
The patch adds a runtime validity check for the user-provided CQ counter offset used in wait_for_interrupt and register_for_timestamp, preventing invalid values from being accepted.
Updates the printk format for div_sel from %d to the correct specifier for a u32, fixing a type‑mismatch in output.

Adds support for additional TC flower filter keys in the Microchip Sparx5 driver’s IS2 VCAP, including IPv4/IPv6 addresses, VLAN info, TCP/UDP ports, TCP flags, and IP TOS, plus a 128‑bit keyfield API for IPv6.
Adds support for Meson S4 SoCs in the meson-gpio IRQ driver, defining extra GPIO IRQ lines and their bank mappings.

The patch adds detection of the PerfMonV2 CPU feature for AMD processors by defining a new scattered feature bit in cpufeatures, based on CPUID leaf 0x80000022, enabling the kernel to recognize and use the new performance monitoring capabilities.
The patch frees the rwi structure after a successful reset, eliminating a 32‑byte memory leak introduced by a prior commit that left the last rwi allocated.
The patch casts __fls's return to unsigned long in the Intel AVS ASoC driver, removing a %ld format warning on arc, m68k and sparc, thus enabling successful kernel builds on those architectures.
The commit renames ice_sriov.c and its header to ice_vf_mbx.c to better reflect their generic virtualization mailbox role and reserve the original name for future SR-IOV specific code.

The patch corrects mis‑accounting of FS_CP_DATA_IO when the data_flush mount option is enabled by splitting the existing cp_task into two structures: cp_task for IO accounting and wb_task for deadlock avoidance, fixing the incorrect checkpoint IO classification.

Adds a guard in ieee80211_tx_control_port() to avoid calling __ieee80211_select_queue() when the device has fewer than four TX queues, fixing a regression that caused invalid queue errors on rt2500‑pci and similar cards.
The commit adds driver support for the Multi‑Gigabit Ethernet (MGBE/XPCS) IP present in NVIDIA Tegra234 SoCs, extending the stmmac Tegra driver to handle this hardware.
Adds missing state strings for __IAVF_INIT_EXTENDED_CAPS and __IAVF_INIT_CONFIG_ADAPTER to iavf_state_str, fixing inaccurate debug output when state transitions are printed.
The commit modifies perf inject to copy the kcore_dir from the input perf.data into the output, preserving kernel symbols and core files for later analysis.
The patch updates the sun4i_can device‑tree binding to reference the common CAN controller binding defined earlier, adding the appropriate include line to the documentation.
The commit relocates Renesas PRR device‑tree binding files from the soc directory to a new hwinfo directory, grouping chip‑ID/SoC information under hwinfo.
The patch removes an explicit cast to u8 in a comparison within the rtl8192e driver, because both operands are already u8 and the macro is a constant, making the cast redundant.
The patch deletes an unnecessary #include of linux/msi.h from the iommu/of driver source file, as the file does not use any symbols from that header.
Adds support for configuring BCH ECC geometry for NAND devices with OOB size >1 KB, trying various ECC strengths or separate meta ECC to keep bad‑block marker in data area.
The patch wraps Energy Model helper functions in CONFIG_ENERGY_MODEL guards, removing unused‑function warnings and avoiding unnecessary work when the Energy Model is disabled.
The patch removes smatch static analysis warnings by initializing variables and adding NULL checks, eliminating uninitialized symbol usage and potential ERR_PTR dereferences in octeontx2 driver code.

The patch modifies the Exynos850 device‑tree DTS to remove wake‑up interrupt entries that were incorrectly duplicated in the main device node, keeping only the proper per‑pin definitions in the wake‑up pin controller.
Adds interrupt configuration and handling to the Micrel ksz9477 PHY driver, matching other Micrel PHYs.
Adds support for the DART page table entry format used in Apple M1 Pro/Max/Ultra (t6000), handling 42‑bit physical addresses and mandatory sub‑page protection by configuring full‑page access.
The patch relaxes checkpatch.pl to accept macros that expand to case statements, preventing spurious warnings about missing parentheses.
Replaces manual size calculation with struct_size() in pwc_decompress, removes flexible‑array sizeof warning and eliminates potential integer overflow that could cause heap overflows.
The patch replaces calls to nodes_weight() with nodes_empty() in arch/x86 where only a presence test is needed, making the check stop early and run faster.

Adds a dma-channel-mask property to the Tegra GPCDMA device‑tree node and updates the interrupts list to include all 32 channels, replacing the previous driver limitation to 31 channels, thereby aligning the configuration with the hardware.

The patch adds runtime warnings that trigger when vendor modules load and any kvm_x86_ops function pointer that should be non‑NULL is still NULL, using the corrected KVM_X86_OP annotations to catch possible NULL dereferences early.

The patch moves the vm_xsave_req_perm call from generic KVM self‑test code into the amx_test, removes it from other tests, and adds a parameter to select the requested xsave bit, simplifying test setup.

The patch updates HDMI driver detection of the hdmi_enable_4kp60 config flag. Previously it inferred the flag via clk_round_rate, which after a clock rework always returned the minimum rate, breaking detection. The change uses clk_get_max_rate to read the clock’s maximum rate, restoring correct 4k@60Hz support.
The patch modifies devm_hwmon_device_register_with_info() to require a non‑NULL 'chip' argument, preventing drivers from merely renaming the old registration function without adapting to the new API.
The commit replaces a left‑shift expression with the BIT macro in the lm90 hardware monitoring driver, solely to make the code more readable; functionality remains unchanged.
The commit adds a PowerPC 64‑bit specific check for the ELF ABI version when loading kernel modules, overriding the generic check to ensure compatibility with potential big‑endian ELF ABI V2 builds.

The commit switches simpledrm from its custom simple‑KMS helper functions to the standard DRM atomic helper APIs, removes unused CRTC atomic enable/disable helpers, and always invokes drm_atomic_helper_check_plane_state(), without altering driver functionality.

The patch replaces an unconditional cancel_delayed_work_sync() in the driver remove() with devm_delayed_work_autocancel(), removing the remove() function because the delayed work may be uninitialized when polling is not used.
Adds a call to type_clear() for devlink ports during cleanup when type_set() was previously used, ensuring proper state reset in the mlx4 driver.
Adds a JPEG decode worker interface to the MediaTek MT8195 driver, enabling three hardware JPEG decoders to run in parallel, extending driver functionality.
The patch updates the cdce925 clock driver to use the new simple I2C probe mechanism with i2c_match_id, removing the unused id argument, aligning the driver with the ongoing i2c probe transition.
The patch replaces a hand‑written delayed‑work cleanup with the helper devm_delayed_work_autocancel(), reducing code size and using the device‑managed API.

The patch moves the handling of the keep_towrite flag from ext4_writepage() to ext4_bio_write_page() so that pages with unwritable buffers retain the TOWRITE tag, preventing race conditions that could cause data loss during writeback.
Moves snapshot lookup to devlink_nl_cmd_region_read_dumpit, removes unused attrs argument, and simplifies early error exit, cleaning up devlink netlink code.
The commit raises the deprecation delay for SELinux's checkreqprot and runtime‑disable knobs from 5 s to 15 s, making the deprecation notice more visible to users still using these options.
Adds support for up to three CAN-FD channels per device in the gs_usb driver, updating the driver to match STM32G3 chips that can provide three channels.
Removes the dead variable 'found_devs' from the qla2xxx SCSI driver, eliminating an unused increment.
The commit deletes unnecessary VPRINTK() debug prints and the ata_scsi_dump_cdb() helper because tracepoints already provide that information, cleaning up libata code.
The commit updates kernel-doc comments in drivers/hv/vmbus_drv.c to correct a prototype name mismatch, eliminating a compiler warning.

The patch removes the mandatory holding of the iscsi driver’s back_lock when calling iscsi_get_task, adding a conditional check to avoid taking the lock on the transmit path, thereby reducing contention and improving performance.

The patch changes DRM EDID logging to use device‑specific debug helpers, adds connector identifiers to messages, passes connector structs more widely, and consolidates tile debug output into a single line, improving log clarity.

The patch refactors pci_power_up() by extracting the post‑delay actions into a new helper pci_set_full_power_state() and calls it from pci_set_power_state(), eliminating redundant work for one caller.
The commit updates the i915 DRM driver to drop Intel Ice Lake (ICL) specific Thunderbolt (TBT) power domain names and use the generic TBT1‑4 names defined by the hardware specification.
Deletes leftover IDE driver documentation files after the driver was removed, cleaning up the doc tree.
The patch modifies amdgpu_display_framebuffer_init to skip the tiling‑flag check when virtual display is enabled, because vkms lacks FB modifiers, eliminating a warning on GFX9+ hardware.
The patch adds a hypervisor check to skip the WBINVD cache‑flush instruction in ACPI sleep handling, preventing a virtualization exception (#VE) on TDX guests.
The patch strengthens tcp_read_sock() by handling unexpected recv_actor() return values, issuing a one‑time warning and ensuring progress to prevent an infinite loop.
The patch changes rhashtable's internal locking from bh‑safe to irq‑safe, allowing the hash table to be used in interrupt context, and updates lock/unlock APIs to pass flags directly.
Adds an explicit length check before memset in vtpm_proxy_fops_read to silence GCC -Warray-bounds warning and ensure the buffer is not overrun, making the code more robust.

The commit updates the yas530 IIO driver to use DEFINE_RUNTIME_DEV_PM_OPS() and pm_ptr() macros, allowing the compiler to drop the dev_pm_ops structure and related functions when CONFIG_PM is disabled, eliminating the need for __maybe_unused annotations.
The commit modifies RTC driver files to include <linux/kstrtox.h> where needed, because the kstrto* functions were moved from <linux/kernel.h> to this new header.

The patch changes the SDMA engine shutdown sequence for SR‑IOV: it disables the engine during hw_fini and re‑enables it when SR‑IOV is active, ensuring the DRM entity is cleared and resume works without other VFs accessing an uninitialized engine.
The commit introduces a generic timeout function interface for the MediaTek JPEG decoder, enabling handling of hardware timeouts.
Adds AMD DRM driver support to enter zstate during extended vblank when FreeSync video mode provides extra blank lines, calculating time gain and updating registers, restoring defaults on exit.

The patch deletes the ipa_fw_mem node from the trogdor device‑tree overlay of the sc7180 SoC because the carve‑out is not used on trogdor boards and its presence triggers a memory‑overlap warning at boot, eliminating the error.
The patch replaces direct rb_next/rb_prev traversal in merge_state with the next_state/prev_state helper functions, simplifying the extent I/O tree handling in Btrfs.

The patch changes the hqd_destroy() callback prototype in the AMD GPU driver, making its third parameter uint32_t instead of enum kfd_preempt_type, matching existing implementations and removing a CFI type mismatch failure when compiled with CONFIG_CFI_CLANG.
The commit modifies the meson-sm1-odroid device tree to set the TF‑IO regulator GPIO to open‑drain, correcting the pin used and eliminating the boot loop that occurs after a reboot.

The patch centralizes and corrects handling of child events when a parent inode has a mark without FS_EVENT_ON_CHILD. It moves duplicated logic into the mark‑type iterator preparation, preventing wrong ignore‑mask clearing and ensuring proper event delivery.

The patch extends NTB EPF support to allow multiple BAR mapping schemes, adding fields to store BAR numbers and handling configurations for config/scratchpad, doorbell, and memory windows, enabling different VID/PID to select appropriate BAR layouts.

Updates the STM32 pinctrl device‑tree binding: renames the property from 'reset' to the correct 'resets' and adds 'additionalProperties: false' to the schema, fixing the typo and tightening validation.
The patch propagates timestamp socket options through the ping6 code, allowing IPv6 ping sockets to request and receive packet timestamps, which were previously ignored.
Adds a new compatible string for Microchip's Icicle reference design in the RISC‑V dt‑bindings, documenting the FPGA fabric version it applies to.

The patch adds error‑path handling in rio_register_mport(): on device_register() failure it calls put_device() and list_del() to release the allocated name and remove the port, preventing a resource leak.

The commit separates kernel‑only capability flags from the user‑visible device_cap_flags by introducing a kernel_cap_flags bitmap, adds explanatory comments, and removes unused kernel flags, clarifying the API exposed to userspace.
The patch suppresses a GCC 12 array‑bounds warning in ath9k's mac.c by adjusting warning levels, likely via a pragma or comment, without altering runtime behavior.
The patch updates KVM’s CPUID handling to clear XFD bits for each state component when the base XFD feature is not reported, ensuring compliance with Intel’s XFD specification.
Adds explicit linux/highmem.h and linux/swap.h includes where needed in the i915 driver, enabling removal of the unnecessary linux/i2c.h include from i915_drv.h.

Adds a flag in the mlx5 driver to track whether the vport ACL namespace has been created, avoiding unnecessary free/reallocate cycles when switching eswitch modes and freeing it only on driver unload or bare metal.

The commit adds support in the bq25892 driver to read the usb_type property from a linked power‑supply device and adjust the input‑current‑limit (IINLIM) accordingly, enabling external charger‑type detection.
The commit replaces uses of SERIAL_XMIT_SIZE with UART_XMIT_SIZE across the serial driver, unifying the macro name to UART_XMIT_SIZE for consistency.
The commit refactors the KVM selftest xapic_ipi_test to stop using vCPU ID macros, switches to vm_create_with_vcpus(), and passes struct kvm_vcpu pointers directly, simplifying the code.
The patch creates nf_nat_ovs.c, moves duplicated OVS and TC NAT functions into it, exports nf_ct_nat() for shared use, and keeps OVS/TC‑specific checks, adjusting protocol handling to work for both.
The patch removes direct calls to the internal function da7219_aad_jack_det() in the rockchip ASoC driver and replaces them with the generic component->set_jack() API.
The patch removes several now‑unused AVIC function prototypes from kvm_x86_ops after they were eliminated in favor of static inline calls, resulting in no functional change.

The commit updates the selftests/bpf/test_lirc_mode2.sh script to return proper non‑zero exit codes on execution failure and to correctly quote a variable for LIRCDEV checking, ensuring skipped tests exit with a skip code.
The patch deletes the redundant enum odm_bw from the r8188eu driver, keeping only ht_channel_width, cleaning up duplicated definitions.
The patch updates the perf test for the CSV output linter, replacing a Python field‑counting script with a Bash function that correctly handles the fewer CSV fields on s390, fixing the test failure.

Adds an explicit gpiolib header include to the Samsung ASoC driver, ensuring required definitions are present and preventing build failures in configurations where the header was previously only implicitly included.

The commit updates the AD4130 driver sysfs documentation to correct Sphinx formatting warnings by reformatting the list of in_voltage‑voltage_filter_mode_available modes into a proper bullet list with blank lines.
Adds support for the RPC-IF module clock on Renesas R-Car V4H (R8A779G0) SoC and fixes table alignment in the related clock definition.

The patch reallocates the SCSI device's budget_map after slave_configure updates the queue_depth, ensuring the map size matches the actual hardware queue depth and avoids unnecessary memory allocation.
The change deletes a register write in init_shader_exceptions() for GV100 GPUs to make the driver match the reference model behavior.

Adds an extensible rseq ABI: kernel now exposes supported rseq feature size and required alignment via ELF auxiliary vectors, allowing user-space to register rseq with struct sizes larger than the original 32‑byte layout.
The commit updates the sun8i-ss crypto driver to replace pm_runtime_get_sync with pm_runtime_resume_and_get, simplifying runtime power management handling.
The patch updates the vt6655 driver macros, renaming the variable wData to reg_value to follow lower‑case naming and satisfy checkpatch.pl style rules.
The patch removes duplicated code by having slave_configure_v3_hw() call the existing hisi_sas_slave_configure() function, consolidating logic.

The commit aligns the function amdgpu_ring_init's prototype in the header with its implementation by renaming parameters (ring_size → max_dw, prio → hw_prio), ensuring consistent naming across the driver.
The patch updates the Bluetooth driver suspend path to always set the event mask after disconnects succeed, even when wakeup is disabled, preventing premature wakeups during suspend.

The patch adds a 1 MiB upper bound for period bytes and uses safe multiplication helpers to prevent integer overflow when allocating the temporary OSS conversion buffer, fixing a reported vmalloc() overflow.
The commit adds support for the Quectel EM05-G USB modem in the option driver, defining its USB configurations and device IDs so the kernel can recognize and use it.
Adds a new power supply driver for the uPI uG3105 battery monitor, integrating it into the Linux kernel's power subsystem; driver operates on x86/ACPI without devicetree support.
The patch updates hugetlb cgroup handling to work with folios instead of pages, modifies __remove_hugetlb_page() accordingly, and deletes an unused helper function.
The patch raises the hard‑reset wait time from 500 ms to 2 s in the Gaudi2 driver to ensure firmware and preboot finish before registers are accessed, preventing premature access errors.
The patch changes the i2c remove callback of the jsa1212 driver to return 0 instead of an error, eliminating a redundant error message already emitted by the driver’s power‑off routine.
The commit moves the fixed file install/remove helpers into the filetable area and changes their API to accept a context instead of an io_kiocb, improving code organization for io_uring.
The commit adds runtime configurability to the Xilinx firmware driver by introducing new IOCTL commands that enable, disable, and query feature settings while the system is running.
Adds documentation for the ti,set-io-isolation property in the wkup-m3-ipc device tree binding, describing its use for IO isolation during low‑power transitions on am43xx platforms.

The patch changes the i915 driver to allocate the scratch page in system memory for all platforms, making the configuration uniform, reducing device memory usage and avoiding device‑side initialization.
The patch disables the allocation of per‑softirq stacks on PREEMPT_RT kernels, saving memory and guaranteeing that do_softirq_own_stack() is never invoked where it is unsupported.
The patch replaces a manual swap operation in the ia64 module with the generic swap() macro from include/linux/minmax.h, simplifying the code without altering functionality.

The patch changes jbd2_submit_inode_data() to use the filesystem‑provided j_submit_inode_data_buffers hook instead of the hard‑coded jbd2_journal_submit_inode_data_buffers, making ext4 fastcommit use ext4_writepages() rather than generic_writepages().

The commit updates device‑tree bindings for the NXP i.MX8MQ VPU, splitting the previously combined G1 and G2 decoder blocks into separate nodes that are independently powered by the vpu‑blk‑ctrl domain.
The patch adds a call to free the allocated soc_dev_attr structure when of_property_read_string() fails in mxs_machine_init(), eliminating a memory leak.
The patch adjusts ov5640_try_frame_interval() to use each mode's max_fps value instead of a hard‑coded 60 fps, fixing incorrect frame‑rate reporting for non‑VGA modes.
The commit updates the MAINTAINERS file to add Helge Deller as the new maintainer for the fbdev subsystem, reflecting a change in responsibility.
Adjusts indentation in the vdpa/mlx5 handle_ctrl_vlan() function to match coding style.
The patch adds handling for power values expressed in micro‑Watts introduced by SCMI v3.1, converting them to the units expected by the Energy Model when needed.
Adds a notifier_block in the random subsystem to inform drivers when a VM forks, with register/unregister helpers and a no-op fallback when the feature is disabled.

The commit removes the Btrfs extent writepage address space callback, which was only used for single‑page writeback from kswapd and never for cgroup writeback, simplifying the code and avoiding inefficient writeback patterns.
The patch deletes a stray comment that was unintentionally added for a not‑yet‑implemented 'arbitrary monitoring target' feature, eliminating confusion without altering any functional code.

The commit refactors ETM4x coreSight code to use named register field macros instead of magic numbers, aligning with sysreg.h naming conventions. No functional change, only style/consistency improvement.
Extracts PAS operations from __mdt_load() into a separate helper, allowing direct calls and simplifying the original function's prototype.
Adds a Chinese translation of docs/zh_CN/vm/page_frags.rst, updating documentation without changing any source code.
The patch replaces the fc_tos field with the new dscp_t type in fib_config and adds validation that IPv4 routes with any ECN bits set in rtm_tos are rejected, preventing mismatched routes.
The patch drops an unused 'task' parameter from arch_prctl helper functions, as they only operate on the current task, simplifying the API.
The patch removes the EXPORT_SYMBOL for kthread_blkcg, limiting its visibility to built‑in blk‑cgroup code only, as the symbol is not needed by loadable modules.

The patch adds three regmap_field helper functions (set_bits, clear_bits, test_bits) to simplify common bit‑manipulation operations, providing a static inline for set/clear and a regular function for test.
The commit updates kernel documentation to mention the existence of count helper APIs for fwnode and device property arrays, clarifying how to obtain element counts.
The commit adds checks for table signatures, checksums, and existence before accessing AMDGPU discovery tables, and temporarily disables the MALL table.
The commit makes several display driver functions static and removes an unused function to silence sparse -Wmissing-prototypes warnings, improving code hygiene.
The patch frees the fw_control_ex structure when pm8001_chip_fw_flash_update_build() fails, removing a memory leak in the pm8001 SCSI driver.
The patch adds a NULL‑pointer check after kzalloc() in the SGI IP22 MIPS driver, ensuring the code handles allocation failures safely.
The commit removes the HMM_BO_SHARE enum/value from the atomisp driver because it is never supported by the hmm_bo code, cleaning up dead code.
Adds a NULL check before iterating over job->bo during error cleanup in the v3d driver, handling the case where v3d_lookup_bos fails and job->bo is NULL, thus preventing a null‑pointer dereference.
The commit rewrites the mixel,mipi-dsi-phy device‑tree binding into a JSON‑schema format, adding properties like assigned-clocks and requiring power‑domains to satisfy dtbs_check.
Adds length checks for the IEEE80211_P2P_ATTR_CHANNEL_LIST attribute in the wilc1000 driver to ensure the buffer is large enough for struct wilc_attr_oper_ch, preventing out-of-bounds writes.
The patch corrects the logic that chooses which DSI port to use for sending VBT packets, using the per‑port bitmask in intel_dsi->ports for dual‑link configurations.

The commit changes the userspace thermal governor's log output, replacing a deprecation warning with an informational message that advises using netlink thermal events, without altering functionality.
The patch updates the MSM DSI PHY driver to replace parent name strings with direct clk_hw pointers, simplifying management and avoiding costly name‑based lookups.
The commit removes the deprecated CHECK macro from the xdp_bpf2bpf self‑test and replaces it with ASSERT* macros, cleaning up the test code.

The patch adds support for configuring the color space on the rkisp1 resizer sink pad and enforces Rec 601 encoding and full‑range quantization when a Bayer format is passed through, ensuring correct handling of raw data.

The commit deletes the IWL_DEVICE_BZ_COMMON macro, which was only referenced inside the IWL_DEVICE_BZ macro, and merges its contents directly, simplifying the macro definitions without altering functionality.
The patch updates rcutorture's torture.sh script to raise its default memory from 1 GiB to 2 GiB and adds handling for a new --kasan option, enabling KASAN testing that requires at least 2 GiB.
The patch updates the DRM Solomon driver to add correct compatible strings for SSD130x I2C displays and deprecates the older strings that included bus/subsystem suffixes.
The patch modifies AMDGPU PSP termination code to free allocated memory even when unload fails, eliminating a memory leak.
The patch adds speed‑bin detection for the A619 GPU in the MSM a6xx DRM driver, allowing the driver to select appropriate frequency ranges based on the specific SKU's clock bin.
The commit moves the STM32MP15_BSEC_NUM_LOWER definition into the stm32 ROMEM configuration, preparing the config for the upcoming STM32MP15 SoC.
Updates mount ID‑mapping code to replace old non‑type‑safe helpers with new type‑safe helpers in mapped_fsgid() and mapped_fuid(), preparing for removal of the legacy functions.
The commit moves the read‑only array range in the v4l2‑ctrls driver from a stack‑allocated variable to a static array, reducing stack usage and slightly shrinking object code size.
The patch removes obsolete s390‑specific compatibility declarations from compat_linux.h after the generic UID16 implementation was adopted, and tidies up the header file.
The patch removes the unused, deprecated <linux/of_gpio.h> include from Mediatek DRM drivers, cleaning up the source as the header is no longer needed.
The commit introduces a new Ethernet driver for the Sunplus SP7021 SoC, adding source files and registration code to support this hardware.

The patch eliminates a use‑after‑free bug in dvb‑core caused by refcount races during device release by checking the dmxdev->exit flag in dvb_demux_open and protecting the exit flag and sync with dmxdev->mutex.
The patch deletes an accidental duplicate definition of tcp_wmem_schedule in the TCP subsystem, resolving a compilation conflict.
The patch adds a check for the return value of alloc_workqueue() in nintendo_hid_probe() and introduces error handling when allocation fails, fixing a missing failure check.

Adds a helper to reset architecture‑specific per‑rmid private storage and invokes it when a new rmid is first allocated, ensuring stale hidden state does not persist across rmid reuse or filesystem mounts.
The commit replaces explicit struct list_head initialization with the LIST_HEAD() macro in the hv utils driver, simplifying the code without altering behavior.
